Crossings therefore fall at t = 7.5k minutes, and 7:00 a.m. is t = 120 = 7.5 x 16 exactly, so the pair DO meet at 7:00 (after two hours P has completed 10 rounds and Q 6, both back at the start). That is what makes the item turn on a single word: strictly BETWEEN 5:20 and 7:00 gives k = 3..15, which is 13; counting the 7:00 meeting gives 14. 'Between' is read as the open interval, so 13. Both printed options 13 and 14 are live, and both passes identified this exact endpoint as the point of dispute before either saw the other.]

49.why: [Adjudicated by hand after the two blind passes split (A said P, B said 'cannot be concluded'). The stem is defective as printed: it states that exactly one suspect is guilty but supplies NO rule about who tells the truth, and the answer depends entirely on which unstated convention is assumed. Under the standard convention for this puzzle type - the guilty person's statements are all false and the innocent speak truthfully - only P survives: if Q were guilty, Q's statement 'R did not steal' would be true, and if R were guilty, P's statement 'Q stole it' would be false though P is innocent. That is the reading the item is evidently built for, since Q's first statement is about R rather than a self-serving denial, which is precisely what rules Q out. Two other readings are defensible on the text as printed: counting the fewest false statements gives Q, and taking the stem strictly literally with no convention at all gives 'Cannot be concluded'. Answer recorded as P with the omission stated rather than hidden.]
